data.argument: TRC’s Q2 print supports the constructive case: revenue rose 71.7% year over year to $14.3 million, led by a $4.6 million increase in commercial/industrial real estate revenue. The company returned to profitability, with net income of $2.6 million versus a $1.7 million loss, while Adjusted EBITDA increased to $8.4 million from $5.7 million. Growth was broad-based, with mineral resources up 20% and farming also higher. Management continues to pursue direct and joint-venture development, including opportunistic land sales. The key limitation is earnings variability: results depend on land-sale timing, leasing, and commodity prices, while current-quarter occupancy, Terra Vista leasing, liquidity, and entitlement milestones were not reported. Peer read-across is mixed, but CHCI and FIP provide supportive development-oriented signals.
key_points: Profitability and Adjusted EBITDA improved materially.
Development thesis remains active, but timing risk persists.
assumptions: Reported revenue growth is a meaningful indicator of near-term execution.
No unreported adverse occupancy, leasing, liquidity, or entitlement developments occurred.
Peer growth signals are directionally relevant despite transaction-timing differences.
